title: `Core\Program::implementing` calls a `private` or `protected` constructor from outside the class.
text: A class with `private function constructor()` is in `Core\Program::implementing<I>()`'s list, and so is one with a `protected` constructor. The call runs the constructor from the top level of the program, where `new A()` is `E0471`, so a class that hides its constructor to control how it is made is created anyway. `implementingWith` does the same. `constructors_of` checks the argument count and not the visibility, and `constructor_fitting`, which `Core\Program::constructors` uses, does check it. It closes when such a class is a diagnostic at the call, as `new` is, with a conformance case.
